overview: This 495-page file traces the 1934 dispute over Japan’s Petroleum Industry Law and a proposed Manchukuo oil monopoly. Embassy reports, company correspondence, and diplomatic cables document objections to compulsory reserves, quotas, and import plans; American, British, and Dutch coordination; and the move toward joint talks with Japanese officials in early 1935.
interest: Company records and diplomatic exchanges reveal how foreign firms and governments coordinated pressure while negotiating Japan’s oil controls.
